quests.sentence: She could swim confidently by the time she was just six years old.
quests.hint: 'Could' is the past form of 'can' - this describes a past ability.
quests.explanation: 'Could swim' is the past form of 'can swim'. The sentence describes an ability she had in the past.

quests.sentence: She can swim thirty lengths of the pool without stopping now.
quests.hint: 'Now' and 'can' together signal a present ability.
quests.explanation: 'Can swim' expresses a present ability. 'Now' confirms this is her current capability.

quests.sentence: After her physiotherapy course, she will be able to run again by next spring.
quests.hint: 'By next spring' is a future deadline, and 'will be able to' signals a future ability.
quests.explanation: 'Will be able to' is the future form of 'can'. 'By next spring' is a future time marker.

quests.sentence: After months of practice, he could finally solve complex algebraic equations.
quests.hint: 'Could' describes a past ability he eventually achieved.
quests.explanation: 'Could solve' is the past form of 'can solve'. 'After months of practice' places the achievement in the past.

quests.sentence: He can now solve most algebra problems without using a calculator.
quests.hint: 'Now' and 'can' together signal a current, present ability.
quests.explanation: 'Can solve' expresses a present ability. 'Now' confirms this is his current skill level.

quests.sentence: By the end of this course, he will be able to take the advanced mathematics exam.
quests.hint: 'By the end of this course' is a future point in time.
quests.explanation: 'Will be able to take' is the future form of ability. 'By the end of this course' is a future time reference.

quests.sentence: Before the training, she could not operate the new accounting software at all.
quests.hint: 'Could not' describes a past inability that has since changed.
quests.explanation: 'Could not operate' is the past form of 'cannot'. The context 'before the training' places this inability in the past.

quests.sentence: She can now operate the accounting system confidently and independently.
quests.hint: 'Now' and 'can' together signal a present ability.
quests.explanation: 'Can operate' expresses a current ability. 'Now' confirms she has this skill at present.

quests.sentence: After the advanced certification, she will be able to train other members of the team.
quests.hint: 'After the certification' is a future condition.
quests.explanation: 'Will be able to train' is the future form of ability. 'After the certification' is a future time reference.

quests.sentence: He could not speak a single word of Spanish when he first arrived in Madrid.
quests.hint: 'Could not' describes a past inability at a specific point in time.
quests.explanation: 'Could not speak' is the past form of 'cannot speak'. 'When he first arrived' places this in the past.

quests.sentence: He can now hold a basic conversation in Spanish with local people.
quests.hint: 'Now' signals his current level of ability.
quests.explanation: 'Can hold' expresses a present ability. 'Now' confirms this is his current language skill.

quests.sentence: After another year of lessons, he will be able to work effectively in Spanish.
quests.hint: 'After another year of lessons' is a future time condition.
quests.explanation: 'Will be able to work' is the future form of ability. 'After another year of lessons' is a future time reference.

quests.sentence: He should have booked the restaurant in advance - it was completely full when he arrived.
quests.hint: 'Should have booked' refers to a past obligation that wasn't fulfilled.
quests.explanation: 'Should have booked' is the past modal perfect. It expresses regret about something that didn't happen in the past.

quests.sentence: He should always book popular restaurants well in advance to avoid disappointment.
quests.hint: This describes a general present recommendation or piece of advice.
quests.explanation: 'Should book' is a present modal expressing advice or recommendation. It describes what is advisable currently.

quests.sentence: He should book early if he wants a table on Valentine's Day next February.
quests.hint: 'Next February' is a future time, and 'should book' gives future advice.
quests.explanation: 'Should book' here expresses a future recommendation. 'Next February' is a clear future time reference.

quests.sentence: She shouldn't have left all her revision until the night before the exam.
quests.hint: 'Shouldn't have left' refers to a past action that was inadvisable.
quests.explanation: 'Shouldn't have left' is the past modal perfect. It expresses that her past action was a mistake.

quests.sentence: Students shouldn't leave important revision until the very last minute.
quests.hint: This is a general present recommendation about study habits.
quests.explanation: 'Shouldn't leave' is a present modal giving general advice. It describes what is inadvisable for students.

quests.sentence: She shouldn't worry too much about the result - she has prepared thoroughly.
quests.hint: 'Shouldn't worry' gives advice about something that is yet to happen.
quests.explanation: 'Shouldn't worry' is a modal expressing future advice. The result hasn't been given yet, so this is future-facing.

quests.sentence: He ought to have replied to the client's email before the weekend.
quests.hint: 'Ought to have replied' refers to an unfulfilled past duty.
quests.explanation: 'Ought to have replied' is the past modal perfect. It expresses that a past obligation was not met.

quests.sentence: He ought to respond to all client emails within twenty-four hours.
quests.hint: This is a general present professional obligation or standard.
quests.explanation: 'Ought to respond' is a present modal expressing a current professional duty or expectation.

quests.sentence: He ought to prepare a thorough proposal before the pitch meeting next week.
quests.hint: 'Before the pitch meeting next week' is a future time reference.
quests.explanation: 'Ought to prepare' expresses a future obligation. 'Next week' confirms the advice relates to a future event.

quests.sentence: They must have taken a wrong turn - they arrived three hours later than expected.
quests.hint: 'Must have taken' is a past deduction based on evidence.
quests.explanation: 'Must have taken' is the past modal perfect used for logical deduction. The late arrival is the evidence.

quests.sentence: When travelling abroad, you must hold a valid passport to enter most countries.
quests.hint: This is a general present legal requirement.
quests.explanation: 'Must hold' is a present modal expressing a current, ongoing legal obligation.

quests.sentence: You must book all required visas at least six weeks before your departure date.
quests.hint: This advice applies to a future journey that hasn't happened yet.
quests.explanation: 'Must book' expresses a future obligation. The advice is about preparing for a future trip.

quests.sentence: She might have over-seasoned the soup - it tasted unexpectedly salty.
quests.hint: 'Might have over-seasoned' is a past speculation based on the taste.
quests.explanation: 'Might have over-seasoned' is the past modal perfect for speculation about a past action.

quests.sentence: The sauce might need a touch more salt and a little more pepper, I think.
quests.hint: This is speculation about the current state of the dish.
quests.explanation: 'Might need' is a present modal expressing present uncertainty or possibility.

quests.sentence: The new restaurant might become very popular once it opens its doors next month.
quests.hint: 'Once it opens next month' is a future event.
quests.explanation: 'Might become' is a future modal expressing a future possibility. 'Next month' is a future time marker.

quests.sentence: According to his prescription, he should have been taking two tablets each day.
quests.hint: 'Should have been taking' describes a past obligation that may not have been followed.
quests.explanation: 'Should have been taking' is the past modal perfect continuous, expressing a past obligation or expectation.

quests.sentence: According to his physiotherapist, he should be doing his exercises every single day.
quests.hint: This describes a current medical obligation.
quests.explanation: 'Should be doing' is a present modal expressing a current obligation or recommendation.

quests.sentence: The doctor says he should be back to full fitness within six weeks.
quests.hint: 'Within six weeks' is a future time prediction.
quests.explanation: 'Should be back' is a future modal expressing an expectation about a future outcome.
